High–Molecular-Weight (HMW) Phthalates

This release contributes to human and ecological exposure, particularly through ingestion of contaminated food or water, inhalation of airborne particulate matter, and dermal contact with PVC-containing consumer goods  [2, 6].

Sources of Exposure
Industrial processes, where high-molecular-weight phthalates are essential plasticizers, represent a considerable source of occupational exposure. Exposure Pathways
Occupational settings represent a critical source of phthalate exposure due to frequent contact with polymer-based materials, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and process intermediates. In these environments, inhalation of airborne particulates and dermal absorption can occur when tasks involve high-volume mixing or maintenance of production lines. However, there is variability in how different regulatory bodies derive these limits, particularly concerning sensitive endpoints such as respiratory sensitization or developmental toxicity. This heterogeneity highlights the need for accurately characterizing exposure scenarios in each industry, as well as employing suitable biomonitoring and control measures to safeguard worker health and reduce phthalate body burdens.
